scope: Solidity bytecode in standalone EthereumJS EVM memory; no transaction objects, provider, live chain or RPC
passed: all ERC721 transfer paths invalidate keys before the new owner explicitly binds them
allowed edge versions are pinned; a changed or withdrawn transit rule cannot silently widen a connection
approved ERC721 operators may transfer but cannot change keys or consent to policies
compiled five-function read ABI and deterministic evidence match the frozen specification
connection endpoint epochs, router epochs and transit status are reevaluated on every view
connection withdrawal cannot be undone by stale approvals and keeps all old edge grants ineffective
connection writes reject unauthorized owners, zero/duplicate/unsorted/missing edge sets and bad limits
connections need two current owner consents and never authorize the reverse direction implicitly
constructor binding rejects absent code and a transit instance bound to another registry
direction, traffic masks, MTU and missing/inactive endpoints fail closed
either endpoint withdrawal versions the rule and cannot preserve the other old consent
inactive owners can withdraw stale policies but the previous NFT owner cannot
invalid zero/equal keys and unknown roles are rejected without consuming ids
missing views are all-zero while ERC721 ownerOf for a missing NFT reverts
network and RPC transports are blocked before tests and dependencies load
one consent never activates a rule, even when both NFTs have the same owner
open registration creates unique owned NFTs with epoch one and no transit
operational key rotation and revocation are owner-only, checked monotonic epochs
removed edge ids are cleared when proposing a new connection version
rotation after the first consent prevents second-side approval until a new proposal
rule ids bind chain, contract, directed endpoints and salt
safe mint callback sees fully initialized state and rejected transfer rolls back the epoch
safe transfer callback sees revoked keys and can only bind new keys as the new owner
seeded lifecycle invariant: no active rule or edge grant survives an unacknowledged epoch change
terms changes reset both consents and expectedVersion prevents stale approvals
the 64-edge boundary is usable and its accepted set remains exact
third parties cannot propose, consent or withdraw even with a predicted rule id
transfer, revoke and reactivation never revive old active transit consents
uint64 key epoch cannot wrap, including during transfer
uint64 policy versions cannot wrap on reproposal or withdrawal
